pr_title: Make Hydrawise poll non-critical data less frequently
pr_body:
## Proposed change
This attempts to fix a problem with rate-limiting of API calls by making non-critical data fetches happen at a reduced frequency.

In particular, this targets "Water Usage Summaries", which get dynamically computed server-side for a given interval (which we request as "current day"). It's not critical that we have this data updated at the same rate as other sensor data, and by reducing the frequency of which we have the server compute the data, we should be able to buy some leniency from the Hydrawise server for regular data polls.

> did you consider using a secondary coordinator for those calls? It might not be ideal, but it could help split out the update logic

That was my first thought as well, but as I started heading down that road I realized how intertwined the two coordinators would be (specifically, the usage summary calls need to know what controllers the user has). Synchronizing state between the two seemed like it would be incredibly error-prone. Alternatively, we could have the non-critical coordinator fetch the other data it needs, but that defeats the purpose of trying to reduce the number of API calls. 

There's also the issue of the entity implementations, which all assume that all data is available all the time, and separating that was going to get really messy.

Oh I see, it's per controller. A future architecture could be that you have 1 coordinator that fetches the user data (+zones) and have 1 coordinator per controller. (Or have multiple coordinators per controller). But I do agree that just splitting out this coordinator into 2 doesn't work nice. 

(this is no must by the way, just food for thought)

review_comments: Does having multiple coordinators really simplify the code? It feels like we are just adding a lot of code that wasn't really necessary in your previous version.

It's not about simplification, it's about correctness. As @frenck pointed out earlier, conditionally fetching data breaks assumptions about what the `homeassistant.update_entity` service call is supposed to do. For example, if you call `homeassistant.update_entity` wanting to get fresh data about a flow sensor, it won't do anything if we're not always pulling data in every coordinator refresh.

While we are on it, can we combine `await self.api.get_user(fetch_zones=False)` and `await self.api.get_zones(controller)` by fetching the zones from the beginning? This would reduce two calls down to one.
In the old days, fetching zones required making separate API calls. But with the graphql API, we can fetch the zone data at the same time as fetching the user data.
We can't combine the two because the GraphQL API returns 502 errors: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/120128
